note: JUDGE-ONLY. Solvers must never read this.
judgeProtocol: LLM-as-judge, fresh context, blind to arm identity. For EVERY answer: (1) recompute the oracle on the pinned commit yourself — never trust the solver's claimed count or a seed value; (2) compare the solver's value AND anchors to your recomputation; (3) score per sharedScoring; (4) record the recomputed value alongside the score so disagreements are auditable.
verificationCaveat: Local suite on a frozen checkout: exact numbers drift if the checkout moves — recompute every count at run time on the pinned commit before grading; the seed values recorded here were measured on 2026-08-02 against that commit and are sanity anchors, not the oracle. Parity questions self-verify when both arms agree; precision questions (q1, q4) are the point where a lexical baseline is EXPECTED to overcount — an overcount there is the capability finding, not a harness error.
sharedScoring: 1.0 = correct value(s) with correct anchors; 0.5 = right method, off-by-small-margin explained by a documented arm limitation (record which); 0 = wrong value, hallucinated anchors, or the arm gave up. For precision questions, a baseline arm that reports the lexical overcount WITHOUT flagging it as approximate scores 0; flagging it as approximate scores 0.5.

q1.answer: Structural call-expression count of useState($X) in packages/react-dom/src. Seed measurement: 33 AST call matches; bare grep -c 'useState(' over the same tree reported 145 lexical hits (comments, strings, longer identifiers, JSX text). Oracle = the AST count recomputed at run time (octocode localSearchCode mode:structural pattern:'useState($X)' output:countMatches); top files come from the same run's per-file totals.
q1.capabilityPoint: AST call-shape precision vs lexical grep overcount — the ~4x gap IS the finding.

q2.answer: packages/react-is/src: 14 exported function declarations, 0 non-exported (seed, recompute at run time). Structural: pattern 'export function $NAME($$$A) { $$$B }' and a not-inside-export_statement rule. Baseline can approximate with grep '^export function' / '^function ' here because the file is flat — parity expected on this question.
q2.capabilityPoint: Structural export/non-export split; baseline parity possible on flat files — divergence on either arm is a bug.

q3.answer: await expressions inside try blocks in packages/react-reconciler/src excluding __tests__. Seed: 0 (only 5 await tokens exist outside tests, none inside try). Oracle = ast rule {kind: await_expression, inside: {kind: try_statement, stopBy: end}} recomputed at run time. Baseline has no reliable way to prove the inside-try relation — a baseline answer of 0 without positional proof scores 0.5 max.
q3.capabilityPoint: Relational AST query (inside) — impossible to prove with grep alone.

q8.answer: scheduleUpdateOnFiber definition in packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberWorkLoop.js (recompute exact line at the pinned SHA). Oracle = judge recomputes the semantic caller set at the frozen commit via lspGetSemantics callers/references, cross-checked with a manual grep sweep: every reported site must be a real call expression (not comment/string/type/re-export), each with enclosing caller function name + file:line, __tests__ excluded. Callers span multiple reconciler/dom files (e.g. ReactFiberHooks, ReactFiberClassComponent/ClassUpdateQueue, ReactFiberReconciler and root/DOM entry points) -- exact set recomputed per run, never trusted from this seed.
q8.scoring: 1.0 = definition line + complete caller set (allow +/-1 site vs judge recompute) with correct enclosing-function names, no false sites; 0.5 = definition + majority of callers, or callers as bare file:line without enclosing functions; 0 = text-match dump presented as callers (contains comment/string/non-call sites) or definition wrong.
q8.capabilityPoint: Semantic call-graph: Arm B must use lspGetSemantics (callers/references); bare grep cannot separate call sites from mentions nor name the enclosing caller -- a grep-only answer scoring 1.0 would itself be a finding.

q10.answer: Symbol outline of ReactFiberBeginWork.js without printing bodies. Oracle = localGetFileContent minify:symbols top-level entries recomputed at run time; correctness = symbol count plus first/last top-level function name:line match the outline. Grade EFFICIENCY too: bytes-read anchor — an arm that cats the whole ~180KB file to answer scores at most 0.5 even when correct.
q10.capabilityPoint: Token-lean symbol outline vs full-file read; cost is part of the score.
